transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, VitalCare), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Diego Ramirez (Head of Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on org/project keys, rate limiting and multi-tenant controls in the Redwood Console and API. Customer asked about quotas, burst limits, per-project billing and security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Demo included Redwood Console view, sample API keys, and how policies map to projects.

Topics:
- Org vs project keys and scoping
- Rate limiting tiers and burst behavior
- Quotas, billing attribution and per-tenant isolation
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO, retention
- Pilot next steps and benchmark planning

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: All right, hello everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. Uh, before we get started, quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here.
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform team.
[00:12] Diego Ramirez: Diego, security.
[00:14] Priya Natarajan: Priya, hi.
[00:16] Alex Kim: Cool. We're gonna show the Console first and then switch to the API examples. Let us know if you want us to pause or dive deeper at any point.

[00:32] Priya Natarajan: OK jumping into the Console, this is the org view. At the top you can see organization-wide quotas, and then we have projects underneath. So one org, many projects, and you can apply policies at either level.
[00:46] Liam O'Connor: Is that per-tenant billing visible? I.e., can we map tokens to our internal cost centers?
[00:51] Priya Natarajan: Yes, you can tag projects and we produce token-level cost breakdowns. You can export CSVs or hook into the cost API.

[01:05] Alex Kim: For rate limits we support both steady-state quotas and burst windows. The Console shows the configured RPS and token-per-minute ceilings, but the API enforces them. Example: you can set a 200 RPS per project with a burst up to 500 for short periods.

[01:22] Diego Ramirez: How deterministic is the burst behavior? We care about spike protection but also predictable SLA.

[01:28] Priya Natarajan: Good question. Burst is token-bucket based; we also let you set a secondary hard limit so if you want no more than 300 at any time you'd set that. For Dedicated customers we can also reserve capacity and guarantee throughput.

[01:48] Maya Chen: Can projects have different models or quantization profiles? We might want cheaper models for internal tooling and higher-quality models for patient-facing features.

[01:56] Priya Natarajan: Yep, projects map to routing policies. You can pin model versions per project and set fallbacks. The Optimize toolkit will recommend quantization profiles per workload.

[02:12] Alex Kim: I'll show org/project keys now. In the Console you can create an org key — that's scoped to all projects — or create project keys which only work for a single project. We also support project-level read-only keys for analytics access.

[02:30] Liam O'Connor: So the token in our app would be a project key? We want to ensure one service cannot consume another project's quota.

[02:35] Priya Natarajan: Exactly. Project keys are scoped for authorization and billing attribution, and they are enforced at the gateway, so no cross-project bleed.

[02:50] Alex Kim: Quick demo of the API: we'll run a sample request with a project key. Note that the sample output here is streaming, but for the purpose of demo the console will show the request metadata including the rate-limit headers we return.

[03:10] [sound of keyboard typing, brief pause]
[03:22] Priya Natarajan: Ok the response includes X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset. We also add a token-cost header so you can see per-request token consumption for cost attribution.

[03:40] Diego Ramirez: Regarding logs, do you produce audit trails per request? We need to map requests to user identities for compliance.

[03:46] Priya Natarajan: Yes we have audit logs tied to the project and API key. In Private deployments you can ship them to your SIEM; for hosted we retain and you can configure retention windows. We support KMS integrations for key wrapping and HSM options for Private.

[04:10] Maya Chen: How about rate limiting and SSO? Can we link SSO groups to project-level permissions?

[04:16] Alex Kim: You can map SSO groups to org roles and control who can create project keys or modify limits. RBAC is in the Console and we support SAML/SCIM provisioning.

[04:34] Liam O'Connor: Any caveats with using org keys in serverless environments? We want short-lived credentials for Lambdas.

[04:41] Priya Natarajan: We recommend project keys and a token exchange flow — short lived tokens issued by your auth service. The Console has a key rotations UI and APIs for rolling keys.

[05:00] Alex Kim: Switching to quotas: you can enforce monthly token quotas per project so cost centers won't exceed budget. We also can set per-route and per-model quotas.

[05:12] Maya Chen: We're interested in a pilot with 3 projects: internal bots, clinician support, and patient messaging. What's realistic for a pilot in terms of throughput?

[05:20] Priya Natarajan: For a pilot we usually provision a small dedicated pool or use hosted with committed burst. Typical pilot sizes are 10-50 RPS per project, depending on expected concurrency. We can run a short benchmark to confirm.

[05:40] Diego Ramirez: On encryption: do you allow customer-managed keys for encrypting model context or logs?

[05:45] Priya Natarajan: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for object storage and database encryption; for runtime KV caches we offer envelope encryption. For Private deployments you can bring your own HSM.

[06:02] Alex Kim: We're hearing a few themes: you need per-project isolation, clear billing attribution, SSO + RBAC, and KMS/HSM options. Anything we're missing?

[06:12] Maya Chen: Data residency — can logs be kept in a specific region? Patient data rules.

[06:16] Priya Natarajan: You can set region preferences for log storage on Private or Dedicated; hosted has region options and we can limit retention. We'll flag that for the pilot.

[06:30] [brief pause, Alex shares link to pricing doc in chat]
[06:36] Alex Kim: I'll highlight a few rate-limit behaviors — we have adaptive throttling if the backend is congested; we can also route to lower-cost model variants automatically based on policy, to maintain availability.

[06:55] Liam O'Connor: How transparent is that routing? We need traceability for any automatic fallback.

[06:59] Priya Natarajan: We log routing decisions and expose them in traces in the Console, so you can see per-request which model variant served it and why a fallback occurred.

[07:15] Maya Chen: Any differences between Dedicated and Hosted around rate limiting?

[07:19] Alex Kim: Dedicated gives you reserved throughput so rate limits are effectively higher and more predictable; hosted enforces shared pool limits but we provide committed capacity options. Policies are the same, but guarantees differ.

[07:35] Diego Ramirez: Can we set different SLA tiers per project? E.g., patient messaging high priority, internal bots lower.

[07:41] Priya Natarajan: Yes, you can assign projects to tiers and priority routing will prefer reserved pools for high tier traffic. Also can set automatic fallback to cheaper variants if high tier is overloaded.

[07:58] Alex Kim: Demo: I'll create a new project and show adding a project key, setting a 150 RPS limit, monthly quota 10M tokens, and linking it to a billing tag.

[08:10] [UI clicks]
[08:22] Priya Natarajan: Notice in the example the project key is created with a read-only toggle for analytics; you can also create ephemeral keys via API.

[08:38] Liam O'Connor: On billing integration — does Redwood push cost usage to our billing system or is it via export?

[08:44] Alex Kim: We currently export usage via the billing API and S3 exports; direct push integrations are in roadmap but we can discuss a custom connector if needed.

[09:00] Maya Chen: Can you show the rate-limit headers again in a high-throughput scenario? We want to see decrement behavior.

[09:06] Priya Natarajan: Sure, I'll run a scripted test. This will hit the project endpoint and you can see remaining counts tick down.

[09:22] [short scripted test runs, audible clicking]
[09:40] Priya Natarajan: You can see after burst the remaining header drops and then recharges over the reset window. The Console charts also reflect the same usage.

[09:52] Diego Ramirez: If a rogue process exhausts a project's quota, does the org get alerts?

[09:58] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we have alerting hooks — email, webhooks, Slack — and you can set thresholds per project. We also have automatic throttling policies and can lock a key if suspicious activity is detected.

[10:18] Maya Chen: Let's talk about org keys again — any reason to use an org key instead of project keys?

[10:22] Alex Kim: Org keys are convenient for admin scripts and cross-project analytics, but for tenant isolation and security we recommend project keys. Org keys are more powerful and should be limited.

[10:36] Liam O'Connor: We use ephemeral ints for serverless. How do rotations work with active sessions?

[10:42] Priya Natarajan: Key rotations are rolling; you can issue new keys and we allow a grace period for the old key. For in-flight sessions the request is validated at the gateway; if a key is revoked the session will fail after the grace.

[11:00] Alex Kim: A few security specifics: audit log retention configurable, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, KMS for keys, HSM on Private. Also we support per-request metadata so you can attach internal user ids which are preserved in logs.

[11:18] Diego Ramirez: We need to validate encryption at rest and in transit; also separation of PII in logs.

[11:24] Priya Natarajan: For PII you can redact or not log payloads; there's a policy to drop or hash sensitive fields before storage. We can also disable payload retention for your projects.

[11:42] Maya Chen: This is helpful. On cost — do you have a worked example for 1M tokens per month across projects?

[11:49] Alex Kim: I'll email a pricing sheet after the call, with sample math for token consumption and reserved capacity.

[12:02] [short pause, Alex types notes]

[12:10] Priya Natarajan: One demo extra: rate-limit overrides. You can create temporary overrides for a project for events or promotions, which expire automatically.

[12:20] Liam O'Connor: Nice. For observability, can we export traces to our Jaeger/Zipkin?

[12:25] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we expose tracing hooks and you can push to your tracing backend. We also have built-in dashboards.

[12:40] Diego Ramirez: Any third-party vendors or integrations we should be aware of?

[12:44] Alex Kim: We integrate with common identity providers, KMS providers (AWS, GCP), and we have partners for on-prem orchestration.

[12:56] Maya Chen: Are there known limitations on model variant routing? For example, if a fallback model doesn't support function calling?

[13:02] Priya Natarajan: Good callout. Routing preserves compatibility; fallbacks are chosen among compatible variants. If the high-quality model used function calling and fallback doesn't, you'd see an error and the request can be routed to a different pool or failover path. We surface that in traces.

[13:22] Alex Kim: We're coming up on time. Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, sample key config, pricing, and schedule a pilot. Anything else?

[13:30] Maya Chen: Please include the data residency notes in the security pack.

[13:34] Diego Ramirez: Also want to see example audit logs and an encryption architecture doc.

[13:38] Alex Kim: We'll include those. Thanks everyone.

[13:44] [meeting ends, informal chatter continues for a few seconds]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mislabels (Redwood sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Infrence") and some punctuation dropped. There was a short period of crosstalk when Liam and Diego asked rapid questions around minute 6.
